method: each finding is produced by a check that runs against files in this repository; the source column names the official page or repository file the check reads. Nothing here is a manual judgement.

findings.check: every JSON file in the repository parses
no unresolved git conflict markers in the tree
the injury snapshot the canonical dashboard publishes is the newest official report

detail.effect: 4 of the five 2026-11-14 team-games the published snapshot marks NOT YET SUBMITTED have since filed, adding 24 player rows

findings.check: the availability state the engine uses and the injury rows it publishes come from the same official report

detail.was: FAIL on 2026-11-14: data/app/report_availability.json was built from the 04:15 AM report and hard-coded deadline_passed_at_capture=False for the five second-night-of-a-back-to-back teams, four of which (NOP, CLE, CHI, MIA) had filed, so out_players_* and out_count_* disagreed.
detail.now: the shared availability file carries the published 06:15 AM ET verdict and snapshot_manifest.json names report_availability_2026-11-15.json (same stamp) as the engine's input; the published injury rows are the 06:15 AM report, so availability state and injury rows come from one official report.

findings.check: an injury refresh can move a published originated line

detail.effect: 0 of 17 price fields moved on 27 lines. Until a minutes-to-value mapping is licensed and validated, injuries inform the reader and not the line.

findings.check: the minutes/production vacuum can be computed for every listed player

detail.effect: The vacuum is a floor. Extending it needs a full official per-player capture, which is a fetch-size decision for the owner (see the questions page).

findings.check: every root-level HTML page is staged into the Pages artifact
